description: When a controller names a box's epoch to the other receivers (RFC 0001 Amendment 24, decision SR-110). A box whose epoch store was lost sends at a random epoch in 4096..61439 (Amendment 23, SR-27); one that rebooted sends a little above where it was. A receiver follows a source only within a window of epochs above the last it heard, so the controller, which hears the box, names the epoch to its modem (SET_PEER_EPOCH) and to every box (CMD opcode 11, params {src, epoch}, see cmd.json). 'rule': a packet of `type` heard at epoch `heard` from a source last known at `prior` (0: never heard) is announced when heard is above prior and either more than `window` above it or, for a source already heard (prior above 0), a HELLO (the box says it has restarted); never when it is not above prior. 'sequences': a PeerEpochs tracker starting empty, in order; a 'heard' step is [source, prior, heard, type, now_ms] and gives whether it is announced now (a source is announced again only at an epoch above the last it announced, so a box repeating its HELLO is announced once); a 'due' step is [now_ms] and gives the [source, epoch] announcements to repeat then (each at the repeat_after_ms offsets from the announcement, one per source per step, however late the step). The Python port (simulator/atalaia_sim/peer_epoch.py) and the Dart port (app/lib/controller/peer_epoch.dart) must give exactly these answers.
